account:
Today I have office business, a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters, tea with my neighbour, and an eighteen to eighteen-thirty meeting in the great hall before going home. I have read today's appointment book. I have just returned to the office with a writable book for the secretary, who is not currently in sight.

The unusual business is the civic hospitality meeting requested by the innkeeper. He says the builder and freight operator will join him to discuss refreshments, deliveries, and hall lighting for community gatherings. He confirmed residents are welcome and need not prepare anything; my neighbour intends to attend. The secretary is to escort me. I saw a lantern appear in the hall yesterday, which could fit the lighting preparations, though I do not know who placed it or why.

More notably, the secretary reports that the committee ordered 120 loaves baked yesterday. That is a substantial order, and its payment remains unconfirmed. Neither the secretary nor I has authorized treasury payment. I have asked her to establish who placed the order, what the bread is intended for, and who agreed to pay. I do not yet have those answers.

My best current explanation is that the innkeeper, builder, and freight operator are arranging some community gathering with food and practical preparations. The bread may be for that, but its precise purpose is unconfirmed. I feel arrangements may be advancing without my knowledge; that warrants questions, not an accusation. I have no direct evidence of wrongdoing or of any purpose other than the hospitality arrangements they described.
